prompt: State the mathematical formula using Pythagoras' theorem for the magnitude of the resultant R of two perpendicular vectors P and Q.

response_structure.guidance: Give the formula relating R, P, and Q.

mark_scheme: 1 mark: R = sqrt(P^2 + Q^2) OR R^2 = P^2 + Q^2.
hints: Perpendicular vectors form the legs of a right-angled triangle whose hypotenuse is the resultant.
teacher_walkthrough: Step 1: State Pythagoras' theorem for vector hypotenuse: R = sqrt(P^2 + Q^2).
lesson_anchors: Perpendicular vectors make a right-angled triangle

abstract_patterns: resolving vectors into perpendicular components and vector addition/subtraction
provenance.independence_statement: Authored independently based on standard Cambridge AS Physics syllabus methods for vector resolution and addition.
